channel.title: Said & Checked: Immigration — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day about Immigration, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Immigration, 2026-11-19: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Markwayne Mullin)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Markwayne Mullin, Secretary of Homeland Security: “Our policy right now is to go after the worst of the worst.” Unsettled. AskAmerica's ICE detention data (TRAC compilation of ICE figures, snapshot of July 11, 2026) show 19,329 of 65,765 detainees convicted and 20,247 with pending charges, about 60% combined; an American Immigration Council analysis of ICE arrest data found most at-large arrests in December 2025 and January 2026 involved people with no criminal record. "Worst of the worst" has no defined threshold, so the evidence does not decide the claim.
  • Markwayne Mullin, Secretary of Homeland Security: “So, when we arrest someone that's on a warrant, most of the time, they're not by themselves.” Unsettled. No official ICE, DHS or inspector general source found describes who is present at warrant-based arrests. Secondary analyses of ICE data put "collateral" arrests at about a quarter of ICE arrests, which is a different measure from the one the statement makes.

3 statements by 2 officeholders. 2 checked: 2 unsettled · 1 not checkable.

item.title: Said & Checked, Immigration, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 1 unsupported, 2 unsettled (Dick Durbin)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “81 percent of Americans support citizenship for Dreamers, including 56 percent of Republicans.” Unsupported. No poll was found reporting both 81% of Americans and 56% of Republicans supporting citizenship for Dreamers. The American Immigration Council's 2018 survey has an 81% figure only for a subgroup of conservative and Republican voters. Searched: the AskAmerica catalog (no polling tables), that survey, and web search results pointing to polls with different wording (legal status rather than citizenship) that were not opened.
  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “Paul Ryan refused to call it or amend it or consider it.” Unsettled. S. 744 died in the House in the 113th Congress, when John Boehner was Speaker; Boehner and House Republicans said it would not get a floor vote (as compiled by Wikipedia). Paul Ryan became Speaker in October 2015. No primary record was read, and the statement may refer to later Dreamer legislation.
  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “I have come to the floor of the Senate over 150 times to share the stories of Dreamers” Unsettled. In the same Nov. 17 speech Durbin calls it his '154th Dreamer story', but that is his own running count; no independent tally of his floor speeches was found, and the warehouse has no floor-speech data.

7 statements by 1 officeholder. 5 checked: 2 supported, 2 unsettled, 1 unsupported · 2 not checkable.
